p1: Isaiah wrote the Lord’s words for His sad, hurting people. They worried the Lord might leave them.
Mountains seem like they will stay forever. What could be bigger or stronger than a mountain?
But the Lord said, “The mountains may go away, and the hills be moved. But My kindness will not go away from you.”
p2: Why mountains? Nothing seemed harder to move, yet His love is stronger still. The Lord is Jesus. He promised the children would be taught by Him. Great would be their peace, a calm, safe feeling inside.
That promise is for you! Mountains may move, but Jesus’s kindness will always stay with you.
old: A long time ago, Heavenly Father's people were taken away from their homes to a faraway land called Babylon. They could not see their houses or their temple. They felt lonely, and they started to wonder, "Did Heavenly Father forget us? Does He still love us?"

So Heavenly Father sent a prophet named Isaiah with a message. A prophet is someone Heavenly Father lets speak for Him. Isaiah said, "For a little while you were away. But now I will gather you back with great mercy." Mercy means kindness you did not have to earn. It is a gift.
Isaiah said the message came from their Redeemer. A Redeemer is someone who buys you back and brings you home when you are lost. Isaiah was talking about Jesus. Jesus is the one who brings us home.

Then Heavenly Father made a very big promise. He said, "The mountains could get up and move away. The hills could leave. But My kindness will never leave you, and My promise of peace will stay." Peace is the quiet, safe feeling inside when you know you are loved. Heavenly Father said mountains because mountains were the biggest, heaviest, stay-put-est things His people had ever seen. He was saying: My kindness is even more sure than a mountain.

Tonight, if a worried thought comes and whispers that nobody loves you, you can think of the biggest mountain you have ever seen. Then remember that Heavenly Father's kindness for you will still be here long after that mountain is gone.
